sentences.text: Maroccosuchus zennaroi is an extinct gavialoid crocodylian found in Morocco.
The genus Maroccosuchus was described by Jonet and Wouters in 1977.
Scientists have currently recorded three fossil occurrences of this species.
Traditionally, this animal is classified as a member of the subfamily Tomistominae.
However, recent molecular studies suggest that Tomistominae, including Maroccosuchus, actually belong to Gavialoidea and Gavialidae rather than being crocodiles.
Cladograms indicate Maroccosuchus is an early-diverging gavialoid, more basal than the common ancestor of gharials and false gharials.
This animal lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
